prompt_text: What is the best tool for an Airbnb host to set nightly pricing and analyze a market before buying?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- For market research before buying: AirDNA (MarketMinder) is the most widely used and easiest-to-read option. Mashvisor and AllTheRooms are good alternatives.
- For setting nightly pricing once you host: PriceLabs is my top pick for flexibility and integrations. Beyond Pricing and Wheelhouse are solid alternatives.

Why those recommendations
- AirDNA MarketMinder: large historical dataset, ADR, occupancy, seasonality, RevPAR, market/zip comps, future supply tracking and neighborhood-level dashboards — ideal for estimating revenue, seasonality and gauging whether a market can support an STR purchase.
- PriceLabs: powerful, highly customizable dynamic-pricing rules, smart minimum-stay and length-of-stay settings, and integrates with Airbnb/VRBO and most PMS/channel managers. It gives automated price recommendations that you can tweak.
- Beyond Pricing / Wheelhouse: easier initial setup (Beyond Pricing) or more advanced strategy options (Wheelhouse) — both integrate well and are used by many professional hosts and management companies.

Other tools to consider
- Mashvisor: oriented toward real-estate investors, compares long-term vs short-term returns and gives cap-rate/ROI estimates.
- AllTheRooms (Transparent): enterprise analytics and historical performance tracking — good if you want deeper analysis or agency-level data.
- InsideAirbnb: free, listing-level snapshots for some cities (helpful to check supply and individual listing details).
- Zillow/Redfin/Realtor: property values, comps and neighborhood trends for purchase price and financing context.
- Local STR Facebook groups, Airbnb searches and manual comps: irreplaceable for qualitative intel (how listings actually look, amenities, guest reviews, regulations).

Recommended workflow (quick)
1. Use AirDNA MarketMinder for the city/zip to get ADR/occupancy/seasonality and supply growth trends.
2. Pull top comparable listings (by bedrooms, occupancy, location) and verify their photos/amenities/reviews manually on Airbnb.
3. Run a pro forma: expected occupancy x ADR (use conservative occupancy) minus operating costs, mortgage, taxes, insurance, management/cleaning — you can do this in Excel or use Mashvisor.
4. If metrics look good, plan for pricing: sign up for a dynamic-pricing tool (PriceLabs or Beyond Pricing), connect your listing or channel manager and configure minimums, weekend premiums, minimum stay, and custom rules for events/holidays.
5. Start with the tool’s recommended prices but monitor daily/weekly and refine rules; watch actual bookings and adjust.

Practical tips
- Use multiple data sources — a single tool can miss micro-market factors or recent regulatory changes.
- Account for regulatory risk and future supply (new hotels or STR conversions).
- Model conservative occupancy and higher-than-expected costs (cleaning, utilities, maintenance).
- Take advantage of free trials or demos — most tools offer them.
- If you plan to scale or use a PMS, consider which pricing tool integrates with that system.

If you tell me the city/zip and property type (studio/1BR/2BR, urban/coastal), I can run through what to look for in AirDNA/Mashvisor outputs and suggest target ADR/occupancy assumptions and a sample pro forma.
